newsitem.title: INDIA: RESEARCH ALERT - Sell India Bajaj - HG Asia.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Sell India Bajaj - HG Asia.

text.p: Securities firm HG Asia on Wednesday recommended investors sell shares of leading Indian scooter and motorcycle maker Bajaj Auto as excess capacities and increased competition were likely to hit margins.
"For the first time the company is facing competition in all products and is finding itself reacting to competitive situations rather than being proactive," analyst Niraj Somaiya said in a report.
He said large increases in capacities by existing players would pull capacity utilisation lower and could lead to a severe price war.
"Overcapacity in all of Bajaj's businesses with the exception of three-wheelers may lead to a price war."
Somaiya said competitors were gaining market share and introducing newer and better products more often than Bajaj.

He said Bajaj's scooters -- which are manufactured based on an older Piaggio design -- were vulnerable to state-of-the-art products introduced by global competitors through their Indian joint ventures.
Somaiya forecast the firm's market share in the scooter segment would fall to 63.1 percent by 1998/99 (April-March) from 68.8 percent in 1995/96.
Increasing demand from rural markets would continue to drive growth in the motorcycle segment, Somaiya said.
"For Bajaj, motorcycles have been the top driver for the last two years and we believe this may continue during the next three years," he said.
But he cautioned that Bajaj faced stiff competition in both the sleek, fuel efficient Japanese models that are made in India and the more rugged models preferred by the rural market.
Sleeker models from Hero Honda, TVS Suzuki and Yamaha would provide the main competition in the upper end of the segment.
Among motorcycles where ruggedness scores over style, Bajaj is represented by the M-80 model.
"Bajaj's M-80 will soon face a severe test in the coming months with Hero Honda launching its step through Street which is Honda's best selling model in the world," Somaiya said.
"Known as Dream in Thailand, it could become a nightmare for Bajaj."
Somaiya said the moped segment would continue to be dominated by TVS Suzuki due to its strong presence in south India which constitutes more than 60 percent of moped sales.
Somaiya said profit after tax (PAT) was expected to climb to 5.46 billion rupees by 1998/99, from 4.4 billion in 1996/97 -- a compound annual growth rate of 11.4 percent.
He said PAT would mainly be driven by non-operating income.
"We believe any earnings surprise is more likely to be negative than positive."
Somaiya said the market expected the company to be among the first to announce a share buy-back as soon as the government approved the scheme.
"But even with expectations of a buyback we do not see the stock outperforming the market," he said.
"With sub-par earnings growth and falling market share the fundamental stock looks weak. Sell the stock," he added.
-- Priya Ramani, Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
